headline: Learned spatial models extend to irregular omics, microscopy, and tomography volumes
label: Learned Spatial Representations In Biomedicine
summary: Coordinate-based and foundation models now address irregularly sampled omics, microscopy, and tomography data with standardized benchmarks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned spatial parameterization of biomedical measurements, where data are represented over continuous or irregular domains rather than only fixed grids. Domain Elastic Transform jointly registers geometry and high-dimensional gene expression on irregular spatial transcriptomics domains using a grid-free Bayesian framework. A reproducible benchmark compares SIREN, Fourier, Haar and grid implicit neural representations on 950 MapZebrain larval zebrafish brain microscopy images. HorusEye, a self-supervised foundation model, restores degraded X-ray tomography across modalities and improves low-contrast lesion detection, addressing restoration rather than spatial representation. The thread therefore holds only partially across the set. What is new is applying coordinate-based and learned spatial models to irregularly sampled omics and to microscopy and tomography volumes, alongside a standardized comparison of representation types.
